source.title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
source.authors: Rhys Gould; Euan Ong; George Ogden; Arthur Conmy

page_placements.theme: Attention heads and MoE experts are polysemantic at the unit level

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies polysemanticity in an attention head, not in individual neurons or MLP neurons as the claim and listed versions specify. Its results therefore concern a related construct rather than testing a listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that Pythia-1.4B attention head L12H0 contributes to several categorized behaviors on natural-language contexts. This is a result about an attention head, not an individual neuron; it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to any listed version.
record.test_reason: The polysemanticity result concerns one attention head (Pythia-1.4B L12H0), not individual neurons. The study's MLP0 neuron analysis covers only the top 16 neurons for one narrow numeric task. It reports no share of polysemantic neurons, no cause, no architecture comparison and no measurement-dependence test for neurons. So no listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present L12H0 as an interpretably polysemantic attention head: successorship predominates, with acronym and greater-than behaviours non-negligible. They call the successorship and acronym behaviours the cleanest example of polysemantic behaviour identified so far in an LLM, and a novel example of head polysemanticity. Separately, they report individual MLP0 neurons as surprisingly interpretable on the narrow numeric task.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes attention-head behavior in language models rather than applying the original neuron-focused methods or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that behavior shares vary with ablation method: resampling versus mean ablation and direct, indirect, or total effect. For example, under indirect-effect ablation the reported shares for successorship are 6.5% with mean ablation and 5.8% with resampling; under direct-effect resampling they are 33%.

fits_no_version.finding: One attention head (Pythia-1.4B L12H0) contributes to several distinct behaviours on Pile contexts: successorship, acronym, greater-than and copying. Shares are 43.4/23.8/18.9% of winning cases and 38.2/10.8/10.5/11.7% of reduced loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some LLM attention heads are interpretably polysemantic, performing multiple distinct functions on natural text.

fits_no_version.finding: Among the top 16 most important MLP0 neurons for numeric succession in Pythia-1.4B, firing is periodic (most often period 10). One feature, f6, appears spread across at least two neurons. Authors call the individual neurons surprisingly interpretable on this narrow task. No rows record this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some early-layer MLP neurons in LLMs encode clean numeric (mod-10) features on narrow tasks, with some features distributed across neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: L12H0 was the winning head on all 64 numbered-list prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Incrementation in numbered lists is mainly carried out by the successor head in Pythia-1.4B.

record.problems: The polysemanticity analysis focuses on one attention head in Pythia-1.4B, not individual neurons. The categorized behavior proportions are presented in figures without uncertainty estimates. The paper notes that its behavior categories are operationalized by specific rules.

untested.parts: No prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons, and no layer comparison, in language models.
Superposition as a cause of neuron polysemanticity is not tested. There is only a remark that feature f6 appears spread across two neurons.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes are not studied.
No activation-function, architecture or regularization comparison of neuron polysemanticity.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not re-examined.
The dependence of neuron polysemanticity on activation range or explanation scoring is not studied. Ablation-method sensitivity is reported only for head behaviour shares.

record.verdict_notes: The row states of 'observed' refer to the head-behaviour measures, not to any version; all rows are correctly linked to none. The MLP0 neuron findings (Section 3.3, Figure 6, Appendix C) are at neuron level but describe interpretable mod-10 neurons for a narrow task, not polysemanticity prevalence. They are logged under fits_no_version rather than as a V2 test.

versions.untested_parts: Vision models and individual image-classifier neurons.
MLP neurons in transformer language models responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how prevalence varies by layer.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity caused by initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Changes in neuron polysemanticity due to activation function, architecture, or regularization, including SoLU or modern convnets, and associated performance costs.
Whether polysemantic neurons resolve into a shared feature or related jobs when examined with better tools.
How neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range or explanation-scoring method.

relation.reason: Section 4.1 and the conclusion discuss head polysemanticity in relation to prior vision and toy-model polysemanticity work. The paper does not test the neuron versions.

tranche.reason: The polysemanticity result is about attention head L12H0, not neurons. The MLP0 neuron analysis covers only the top 16 neurons on a narrow numeric task. There is no share of polysemantic neurons, no cause test and no architecture or measurement comparison.

source_check.notes: The polysemantic unit is attention head L12H0, not an MLP neuron. The Figure 11 greater-than and copying values (10.5, 11.7) are reconstructed from garbled extracted text, and the shares sum to 99.9%. Copying is negligible in winning cases (Figure 10 caption).
